text:
maria_g: hey team, noticed dedicated pool started queueing requests way before expected headroom was exhausted this morning. committed rps is 600 but we started seeing >200ms enqueue times when avg qps was ~350.

maria_g: headers from a failing request: `X-Reserved-Pool: rp-678`, `X-RateLimit-Limit: 600`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 120` — but app logs show ~220 rps for that key.

tom_h: hmm, can you paste a short repro? curl or SDK call that hits the dedicated pool?

maria_g: minimal repro below. this is hitting our dedicated model endpoint: 
```bash
for i in {1..400}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/rp-678/generate &
  sleep 0.002
done
wait
```
we see ~350 qps overall but the service starts queueing after ~2 minutes.

jesse_s: are you using a shared API key mapped to a tenant? billing system sometimes switches keys to a different reserved pool during commits.

maria_g: key is tenant-scoped, rp mapping was stable AFAICT. billing-bot did send a notice yesterday about plan bump but we didn't change keys.

billing-bot: FYI: invoice #INV-2024-0821 shows customer upgrade effective 2024-11-07 02:00 UTC; no key rotation performed.

infra-bot: Autoscaler snapshot for rp-678 around incident: replicas=4, qlen=38, avg_latency=180ms, token_bucket.tokens=0, refill_rate=600rps, window=60s.

tom_h: token_bucket.tokens=0 while avg qps << refill_rate suggests per-shard allocation or handshake mismatch. do you have per-route SLO routing enabled?

maria_g: yes we enabled per-route latency SLOs last week for streaming endpoints. Could that trigger fallback to a lower-capacity fallback pool?

jesse_s: it's possible. SLO routing can pin requests to a fallback variant during health oscillation. That fallback might be in the same reserved pool but limited by per-route caps.

maria_g: any quick checks I can run?

tom_h: 1) check request routing headers `X-Route-Variant` on responses 2) inspect `rb-commit` and `rb-headroom` labels on the pool nodes 3) confirm the key's assigned `capacity_group` in the control plane.

maria_g: ran a grep on response headers, saw `X-Route-Variant: svc-v2-fallback` for ~20% of sampled requests around the enqueue spike.

infra-bot: pool node labels: `rb-commit=600`, `rb-headroom=72`, `zone=us-west-2a`. Some nodes report `reserved_pool_quota=480` due to active maintenance shard gating.

tom_h: maintenance shard gating explains the effective lower capacity (480 vs 600). when a shard is drained we keep headroom but commit visible in control plane can be stale. that causes token bucket to hit zero earlier.

jesse_s: confirm if the customer's SLA requires continuous commit or allows short maintenance. also check if the fallback variant has a stricter per-route cap (e.g., 200rps).

maria_g: SLA is 99.95% latency with 90% of requests under 300ms. maintenance window should have been off-peak. customer is upset because they saw elevated latency during business hours.

tom_h: next steps: (a) correlate maintenance window timestamps with billing and deploy logs (b) replay routing decisions for affected traces (`trace_id` list from app logs) (c) escalate to runtime ops to re-evaluate shard gating timing and node replacement cadence.

maria_g: posted a sample trace id: `trace-20241107-8731`. logs show `route_decision=fallback` at 02:14:22 UTC.

infra-bot: runtime note: node replacement started at 02:10:17 UTC due to GPU driver patch; drained one shard (shard-3) and moved traffic. autoscaler prevented immediate spin-up to avoid overcommit.

jesse_s: can we check billing flags? sometimes a sudden plan change triggers a temporary throttling policy while entitlement propagation completes.

billing-bot: entitlement propagation for upgrade INV-2024-0821 completed at 02:05:40 UTC. no throttles applied by billing service.

tom_h: sounds like a maintenance gating + fallback variant cap combined. mitigation: (1) runtime ops to mark gating as maintenance-critical so new replicas spin up faster, (2) temporarily raise fallback per-route cap for this tenant to match 600 while we stabilize, (3) postmortem + customer comms.

maria_g: can infra ops do a quick revert to reduce drain aggressiveness? we need to restore effective capacity to avoid SLA breaches.

infra-bot: will attempt a controlled cancel of shard drain; ETA 8 minutes. will also open a hotfix to adjust `drain_threshold` for dedicated pools.

maria_g: thanks. I'll prepare a short explanation for the customer and include expected timeline.

jesse_s: when you send comms: mention that no billing throttle was applied, root cause is maintenance-driven shard gating causing effective capacity dip and fallback routing; remediation is done and we will add safeguards. :+1:

maria_g: noted. I'll ping here once infra confirms cancel complete.

infra-bot: shard drain cancel completed at 02:20:13 UTC, replicas back to 5, token_bucket.tokens refilled, enqueue times dropping under 20ms.

maria_g: confirmed latency recovered. closing loop with customer now. thanks all. :heart:
